actions: Retried public resolution of Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.16441066 through the peer-reviewed article DOI link, exact-record web searches and public mirrors. The article still explicitly states that all simulation/analysis code is deposited at that Zenodo DOI, but the current web transport failed at the DOI-to-Zenodo redirect and did not expose the record file list/checksums.

Repeated exact-title/DOI/author searches for a non-author rerun or failure report. Accessible results were the original paper/preprint/author pages and generic indexes; no clear independent reproduction was established.

Extracted version-of-record details for a stricter source-derived control: each pretrained module is a 512-neuron leaky RNN with ReLU and per-step layer normalization; Direction pretraining uses T=100 binary moving-bar clips over 12 directions with sparse Bernoulli noise p=0.01; representation PR is (sum eigenvalues)^2/sum(eigenvalues^2); perturbations include frame dropout and random interpolation that destroys spatial locality while preserving pixel-intensity statistics.

Extended the previous 2-D trajectory control to paper-like binary moving-bar videos. Training used 12 direction classes, 14 frames, 12x12 binary frames, sparse p=0.01 pixel noise, and a deliberately strong direction-correlated absolute starting-position shortcut. Test starts were randomized independently of direction. Five independent training seeds, 2,000 train and 800 test clips per seed.

Compared a raw pixel GRU (10,212 parameters), a translation-normalized recurrent control using frame-centroid tracks relative to the first frame projected into an otherwise matched GRU (10,500 parameters), and a parameter-matched non-recurrent temporal MLP on the same relative centroid tracks (10,643 parameters).

Raw GRU achieved 90.40% mean IID accuracy under the correlated-start training distribution but collapsed to 17.85% when start position was randomized. Translation-normalized GRU retained 53.48%; the parameter-matched non-recurrent temporal MLP retained 68.93%.
Under unseen speed 0.65x/1.35x, translation-normalized GRU obtained 43.43%/57.03% and the matched non-recurrent MLP 59.08%/66.75%; raw GRU remained 16.28%/9.43%.

With 30%/60% frame-drop-and-hold, translation-normalized GRU scored 52.43%/48.18% and the matched non-recurrent MLP 62.00%/51.90%; with a fixed-length random-interpolation analogue at 30%, recurrent translation-normalized control scored 49.20% and non-recurrent MLP 46.88%.

Sequence-level representation participation ratio remained low in both normalized models: on randomized-start clips PR 2.61 for normalized GRU and 2.91 for matched non-recurrent MLP, versus raw GRU PR 3.34. The non-recurrent model's stronger clean/speed/dropout performance means low-dimensional primitive isolation is again sufficient in this simplified regime; recurrence showed a small relative advantage only under the interpolation corruption.

public_sources.title: Representation Transfer via Invariant Input-driven Continuous Attractors for Fast Domain Adaptation

public_sources.source_fact: RNN update uses leaky recurrent ReLU plus per-step layer normalization and truncated BPTT/Adam 1e-4; 512 neurons; Direction clips T=100, 12 directions, p=0.01 sparse Bernoulli noise.

Participation ratio PR=(sum lambda_i)^2/sum lambda_i^2. Paper robustness tests use frame dropout and random interpolation; controlled direction+position representation has effective dimension 7.7 and poorer transfer than direction-only (~2.11).

design.train_nuisance: absolute starting position strongly correlated with direction
design.dropout: selected frames held at previous frame
design.random_interpolation_analogue: selected interior frame replaced by shuffled pixels drawn from adjacent frames while keeping sequence length fixed

translation_normalized_gru.preprocessing: per-frame active-pixel centroid trajectory minus first-frame centroid, then learned 2-to-144 projection into matched GRU

translation_normalized_nonrecurrent_mlp.preprocessing: same relative centroid trajectory; flattened temporal MLP

scope: This is source-derived, not an exact reproduction of the peer-reviewed PRG architecture or DVS/RGB downstream task.
Centroid-relative normalization is a strong hand-designed geometric prior and uses a much lower-dimensional sufficient statistic than the paper's learned 512-neuron manifold.
Random interpolation is a fixed-length analogue rather than the paper's inserted-frame protocol.
The train-time direction-position shortcut was deliberately constructed to stress entanglement and is not claimed to match the paper's synthetic distribution.

Results support low-dimensional primitive isolation as sufficient in this simplified binary-video regime and weaken any claim that recurrence/continuous-attractor dynamics alone explain robustness; they do not show recurrence is unnecessary in the real DVS/RGB system.

The normalized recurrent model modestly outperformed the matched non-recurrent MLP under the interpolation corruption, so recurrence may still provide temporal robustness not captured by this control.

evidence_added_this_run: Binary-video nuisance-shift control: raw GRU 90.40% IID -> 17.85% randomized-start, while translation-normalized GRU retained 53.48% and a parameter-matched non-recurrent temporal MLP 68.93% across five seeds.

Under speed shift and frame dropout the parameter-matched non-recurrent normalized control usually exceeded the normalized GRU; normalized GRU only led on the random-interpolation analogue (49.20% vs 46.88%).

Both normalized representations stayed low-dimensional (random-start PR 2.61 recurrent, 2.91 non-recurrent), close in spirit to the paper's reported direction-only PR ~2.11 and far below its mixed direction+position PR 7.7, although these PRs are not directly comparable because the architectures/data differ.
candidate_update.interpretation: Across two successive source-derived controls, explicit nuisance removal/primitive isolation is sufficient to reproduce strong shift robustness without an attractor-specific mechanism. The remaining credible attractor-specific hypothesis is narrower: recurrence may add robustness to temporally destructive perturbations or real event/video dynamics after low-dimensional primitive isolation. Exact artifact audit and real-data matched ablation remain necessary.

exact_next_action: Keep trying public metadata/file-list resolution for Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.16441066 and exact-title/citation searches for a non-author rerun. If the artifact remains inaccessible, construct a stricter recurrence-specific causal control on the binary-video task: use identical translation-normalized input and parameter-matched recurrent versus non-recurrent temporal models, train/evaluate with the paper's inserted-frame random-interpolation protocol rather than the fixed-length analogue, sweep corruption level and temporal gap length, and add hidden-state contraction/recovery measurements. If recurrence advantage survives only temporally destructive perturbations, quantify the boundary and then seek the same signature in public DVS-style data.
